mainTopic: Consecrating an addition to the עזרה and ירושלים: why the שתי הלחם can't be used, the songs sung, using פסוקים for protection, and the procession of the two תודות.
overview: The גמרא looks for a leavened offering to use when consecrating a new addition to the עזרה. Leavening the שירים of a regular מנחה is forbidden. The שתי הלחם of שבועות are leavened, but every possible timing fails, so the גמרא concludes it is impossible. It then turns to the songs sung at the consecration: תהלים 100 with instruments, ארוממך, and the 'song of פגעים' (תהלים 91 and תהלים 3). This leads to רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said these verses at bedtime. The גמרא explains that using פסוקים for protection is allowed, healing with them is forbidden, and spitting and then saying them costs a person עולם הבא. Next, the גמרא explains that in the procession the two תודות walk ahead of the בית דין. It brings a מחלוקת over whether the תודות walked side by side or one behind the other, and over what 'the inner one' means. It challenges the side-by-side view from the משנה's rule that the inner one is eaten, but shows the same question applies to both views. רבי יוחנן then begins a new explanation, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Leavening the leftovers of a meal-offering is not allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the idea of leavening the שירים of a מנחה and using them for the consecration. It rejects this idea from a פסוק as explained by ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that he makes the leftovers leavened and uses them to consecrate, that does not work. The Torah says 'it shall not be baked leavened, their portion,' and ריש לקיש explained that even the כהנים' portion may not be baked as חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one way to get leavened bread for the consecration and immediately knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is to take the part of a מנחה that the כהנים eat and bake it as חמץ. ריש לקיש reads the פסוק to mean that even the כהנים' portion must not be חמץ. So this way of getting leavened bread is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftovers of a מנחה, which the כהנים eat
Consecrates (here, a new part of the עזרה)

phrases.english: And if you say that he leavens the leftovers
phrases.notes: The leftovers are the part of the מנחה the כהנים eat after the handful is burned.

phrases.english: and consecrates with them —
but isn't it written: 'It shall not be baked leavened, their portion'?
And ריש לקיש said:
Even their portion may not be baked leavened!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier search for a leavened offering to use for the consecration.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects leavening the שירים of a מנחה as a way to consecrate.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק, as explained by ריש לקיש, forbids baking even the כהנים' portion as חמץ.

steps.title: Why not use the two loaves of שבועות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back and asks why the שתי הלחם of עצרת, which really are leavened, could not be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? It is possible to consecrate with the שתי הלחם on עצרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that no suitable leavened offering exists. It points to the שתי הלחם, which the Torah itself commands to be חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the leftovers of a regular מנחה, the שתי הלחם are supposed to be leavened, so the problem from ריש לקיש does not apply. The question is why they would not be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The two leavened loaves brought on שבועות
The name the חכמים use for שבועות

phrases.english: Why not?
It is possible to consecrate with the two loaves on Shavuot!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְּמָה לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שירים option is rejected, it offers another leavened offering.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a regular leavened מנחה cannot be used
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שתי הלחם are leavened by Torah command, so the ריש לקיש problem should not apply to them.

steps.title: It cannot be done
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers briefly that using the שתי הלחם is simply not possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer, and it is setting up the next steps, which explain why it cannot be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not say the שתי הלחם would be invalid in principle. It says that the timing cannot be made to work in practice.

phrases.english: Because it is not possible.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the שתי הלחם.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שתי הלחם could be used, since they are leavened.
steps.terutzMaskana: The timing makes it impossible, as the next steps explain.

steps.title: Building and consecrating the day before does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests the first timing option: build and consecrate on ערב שבועות. This fails because the loaves are not holy until the lambs are slaughtered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could we do it? Should we build it the day before and consecrate it the day before? The שתי הלחם only become holy through the slaughter of the lambs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining why it cannot be done by trying the first timing option and showing that it fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שתי הלחם only become fully holy when the two lambs brought with them are slaughtered. That happens on יום טוב itself. On the day before, the loaves are not yet holy enough to be used for the consecration.

keyTerms.meaning: From yesterday, meaning the day before
The slaughter of the lambs brought with the loaves

phrases.english: How could we do it?
Should we build it the day before and consecrate it the day before?
The two loaves, through the slaughter of the lambs,
that is when they become holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי נֶיעְבֵּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining why it is not possible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Build and consecrate on ערב שבועות.
steps.terutzMaskana: This fails, because the loaves are not yet holy before the lambs are slaughtered on יום טוב.

steps.title: Building the day before and consecrating on יום טוב does not work either
steps.stepSummary: The second timing option is to build before יום טוב and consecrate on יום טוב. This also fails, because the consecration must happen at the time of the building.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we build it the day before and consecrate it now, on יום טוב? We require the consecration to be at the time of the building.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second timing option, building before יום טוב and consecrating on יום טוב, and rules it out. More options follow in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This option avoids the problem from step 4, because on יום טוב the loaves are already holy. But the consecration must happen when the building is completed, not a day later, so building the day before and consecrating on יום טוב fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecration at the time of the building

steps.whatToRemember: The consecration must happen at the time the building is completed, so the building and the consecration cannot be split across two days.

phrases.english: Should we build it the day before and consecrate it now?
We require consecration at the time of the building.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵינַן קִידּוּשׁ בִּשְׁעַת הַבִּנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second timing option, after building and consecrating on ערב שבועות failed in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Build before יום טוב and consecrate on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The consecration must happen at the time of the building, so this option fails as well.

steps.title: Building and consecrating on יום טוב itself
steps.stepSummary: The third timing option is to build and consecrate on יום טוב itself. It fails because building the מקדש does not override יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe build it on יום טוב and consecrate it on יום טוב? No, because building the מקדש does not push aside יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another timing: do both the building and the consecrating on יום טוב, when the loaves are holy. It rejects this right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This option solves the problems from the last two steps, because the loaves are holy and the building and consecrating happen together. But building is מלאכה, and building the מקדש is not allowed on יום טוב. So this option also fails.

phrases.english: Let us build it on the Festival
and consecrate it on the Festival?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בִּנְיַן מִקְדָּשׁ דּוֹחֶה יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: The building of the Temple does not override the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִבְנְיֵיהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב וּנְקַדְּשֵׁיהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third timing option, after the two options in steps 4 and 5 failed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting a proposed scenario with a halachic rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Do everything on יום טוב, when the loaves are holy
steps.terutzMaskana: Building the מקדש is not allowed on יום טוב

steps.title: Waiting until after יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The fourth option is to wait until after יום טוב and then build and consecrate. It fails because the loaves become invalid once they are left overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe leave it until afterward and then build and consecrate? No, the loaves have already become invalid from being left overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests waiting until יום טוב is over and then doing the building and consecrating together. It rejects this because the loaves will no longer be valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This avoids building on יום טוב. But the שתי הלחם must be eaten by the end of the night after they become holy, so by the next day they are invalid from לינה. Invalid loaves cannot be used for the consecration.

keyTerms.meaning: Being left overnight past the proper time, which makes קדשים invalid

phrases.english: Let us leave it until afterward,
and then build it and consecrate it?
They have become invalid by being left overnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׁבְּקֵהּ לְבָתַר הָכִי, וְנִבְנְיֵיהּ וְנִיקַדְּשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth timing option, avoiding the problem of building on יום טוב
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting a proposed scenario with a halachic rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wait until after יום טוב to build and consecrate
steps.terutzMaskana: By then the loaves are invalid from לינה

steps.title: Finishing the building right after יום טוב ends
steps.stepSummary: The last option is to build almost everything before יום טוב and finish the last bit right after יום טוב ends, before the loaves become invalid. It fails because the מקדש may not be built at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe build it before יום טוב, leave a little unfinished, and the moment יום טוב ends, finish it and consecrate it? No, the מקדש is not built at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one last clever plan: leave only a small part to finish the moment יום טוב ends, while the loaves are still valid. It rejects this because that moment is nighttime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This plan tries to avoid all three earlier problems: no building on יום טוב, building and consecrating happen together, and the loaves are still valid that night. But יום טוב ends at night, and building the מקדש at night is not allowed. The next step brings the source for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: On the eve of the day, before the Festival

phrases.english: Let us build it on the eve of the Festival
and leave a little of it unbuilt
so that as soon as the day is over
phrases.notes: Literally 'until the day becomes holy.' He means the moment יום טוב ends and the next day begins at night.

phrases.english: we immediately finish it and consecrate it?
The Temple is not built at night;

steps.triggerLanguage: נִבְנְיֵיהּ מִמַּעֲלֵי יוֹמָא וּנְשַׁיַּיר בֵּיהּ פּוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final timing option, built to avoid the problems found in steps 5, 6 and 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting a proposed scenario with a halachic rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Finish the last bit of building the moment יום טוב ends, while the loaves are still valid
steps.terutzMaskana: The מקדש may not be built at night

steps.title: אביי's source that the מקדש is not built at night
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves from the פסוק 'And on the day that the משכן was set up' that the משכן, and so the מקדש, is set up only by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As אביי said: How do we know the מקדש is not built at night? Because it says 'And on the day the משכן was set up': by day you set it up, at night you do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings אביי's source for the rule it just used: building the מקדש only happens by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the משכן was set up 'on the day'. אביי reads that word as a rule: setting up the משכן, and so building the מקדש, is a daytime activity only. This backs up the rejection in step 8.

phrases.english: as Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בַּלַּיְלָה?
phrases.english: From where do we know that the Temple is not built at night?
As it says: "And on the day that the Tabernacle was set up"
by day one sets it up,
at night one does not set it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the rule used in step 8
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the מקדש is not built at night
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 9:15, 'And on the day that the משכן was set up', as read by אביי

steps.title: Using the שתי הלחם is impossible
steps.stepSummary: Since every timing option fails, the גמרא concludes that the שתי הלחם cannot be used for the consecration.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the whole discussion: there is no workable way to use the שתי הלחם, which is exactly what it claimed in step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 said briefly that the שתי הלחם cannot be used. Steps 4 through 9 tested every timing and found a problem with each one. Now the גמרא returns to that claim, fully proven.
steps.whatToRemember: The שתי הלחם can't work: before יום טוב they aren't holy yet, consecrating must happen with the building, building isn't allowed on יום טוב, after the night they are invalid from לינה, and building at night isn't allowed.

phrases.english: Therefore, it is not possible.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכָּךְ לָא אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the testing of all timing options and confirms the answer in step 3
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The שתי הלחם cannot be used to consecrate an addition to the עזרה.

steps.title: The songs and instruments at the consecration
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's words 'and with song'. A ברייתא lists the songs sung, the instruments played, and where they were played.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And with song.' The Rabbis taught: the song of thanksgiving was sung with harps, lyres and cymbals at every corner and on every large stone in ירושלים. They also said 'I will extol You, ה׳, for You have lifted me up', and the song against harmful spirits; some call it the song of plagues.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new phrase in the משנה, 'and with song', and brings a ברייתא that explains what that song was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic. The ברייתא describes the ceremony: the song of thanksgiving with music all over ירושלים, plus two more chapters of תהלים. The last song has two names, 'song of harmful spirits' or 'song of plagues'.

phrases.english: And with song.
The Rabbis taught:
The song of thanksgiving
phrases.notes: This is תהלים 100, which opens 'A psalm of thanksgiving'.

phrases.english: with harps, lyres, and cymbals
at every single corner
and upon every large stone in Jerusalem,
and one says: "I will extol You, O Lord, for You have lifted me up, etc."
and the song of harmful spirits,
phrases.notes: This is תהלים 91, 'He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High'.

phrases.english: and some say: the song of plagues.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְשִׁיר. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁיר שֶׁל תּוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שתי הלחם discussion and starts explaining the next phrase of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The consecration was done with the song of thanksgiving and instruments throughout ירושלים, plus 'ארוממך' and the song of harmful spirits (or plagues).

steps.title: Why the song has two names
steps.stepSummary: One name, 'of נגעים', comes from the פסוק about plagues not coming near your tent. The other name, 'of פגעים', comes from the פסוק about a thousand falling at your side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever calls it the song of נגעים learns it from 'No plague shall come near your tent.' Whoever calls it the song of פגעים learns it from 'A thousand shall fall at your side.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where each of the two names for the same song comes from. Each name is tied to a different פסוק in the same chapter of תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both names describe the same chapter (תהלים 91). It just depends which פסוק you focus on: one speaks of plagues (נגעים), the other of harmful attackers falling away (פגעים).

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (a way of presenting each side of a disagreement)
Harmful forces or spirits that attack

phrases.english: The one who says it is the song 'of plagues':
because it is written: 'And no plague shall come near your tent.'
And the one who says it is the song 'of harmful spirits':
because it is written: 'A thousand shall fall at your side.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר דִּנְגָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two names for the song mentioned in the ברייתא of step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both names come from פסוקים in תהלים 91: נגעים from 'ונגע לא יקרב', פגעים from 'יפל מצדך אלף'.

steps.title: Which verses are said
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא spells out the text: תהלים 91 from 'יושב בסתר עליון' through 'כי אתה ה׳ מחסי', and then all of תהלים 3.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says from 'He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High' until 'For You, ה׳, are my refuge.' Then he goes on to say 'A psalm of דוד when he fled from his son אבשלום' until 'Salvation is to ה׳; Your blessing is on Your people, סלה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and lists exactly which verses make up this song. It is part of תהלים 91 followed by the whole of תהלים 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From תהלים 91 they say only up to פסוק 9, not the whole chapter. Then they say all of תהלים 3, which ends at 'לה׳ הישועה'. Both passages are about ה׳ protecting a person from danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Until (the recital goes up to here)
And then he goes on to say

phrases.english: And he says: 'He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High'
'shall rest in the shadow of the Almighty,'
until 'For You, the Lord, are my refuge;'
'You have made the Most High Your dwelling.'
And then he goes on to say:
'A psalm of David, when he fled'
'from Absalom his son.'
'Lord, how many are my enemies,'
until 'Salvation belongs to the Lord;'
'Your blessing is upon Your people, Selah.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 3:9, the last פסוק of that chapter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר: יֹשֵׁב בְּסֵתֶר עֶלְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and gives the actual text of the song just named.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The song is תהלים 91:1–9 followed by all of תהלים 3.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'song of פגעים' is תהלים 91 (up to 'כי אתה ה׳ מחסי') plus תהלים 3.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי said these verses at bedtime
steps.stepSummary: We are told that רבי יהושע בן לוי used to say these verses and then go to sleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי would say these verses and then lie down to sleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what an אמורא actually did with these verses. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying these verses before sleep shows he used them for protection. That practice is about to be questioned against another statement of his own.

keyTerms.meaning: And he would lie down to sleep

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר לְהוּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi would say
these verses, and then go to sleep.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר לְהוּ לְהָנֵי קְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the Temple song to a personal practice of using the same verses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע בן לוי recited these protective verses before sleeping.

steps.title: Isn't healing with Torah forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how he could do this, since he himself said it is forbidden to heal oneself with Torah words.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do that? Didn't רבי יהושע בן לוי himself say: It is forbidden to heal oneself with words of Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי's practice using his own ruling. His practice seems to contradict what he taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using פסוקים as a remedy turns Torah into a kind of medicine, which he forbade. Saying verses so nothing bad happens at night looks like the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say...? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: How could he do this?
But didn't Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:
It is forbidden to heal oneself with words of Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the practice described in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's practice of reciting the verses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own ruling forbids healing with Torah words, and reciting verses for safety seems to be the same kind of use.

steps.title: Protecting is different from healing
steps.stepSummary: The answer: using verses to protect yourself is different from using them to heal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Protecting is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction in two words. Saying verses for protection is allowed, even though healing with them is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is on using Torah to cure something that is already wrong. Asking for protection before anything happens is a different act, so his practice is fine.

phrases.english: To protect is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהָגֵן שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any use of פסוקים for physical benefit is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only healing is forbidden; reciting verses for protection is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Saying פסוקים for protection is allowed; using them to heal is what רבי יהושע בן לוי forbade.

steps.title: If there is a wound, is it only 'forbidden'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says: then 'forbidden' must mean when there is already a wound. But a משנה says whispering over a wound costs one his share in עולם הבא, which is far worse than just 'forbidden'.
steps.simpleTranslation: So when he said 'forbidden', it was where there is a wound? But if there is a wound, is it just forbidden and nothing more? We learned in a משנה: One who whispers over a wound has no share in the World to Come!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא follows the answer through: 'forbidden' must refer to someone with a wound. Then it challenges this with a משנה that treats that case much more harshly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If healing means saying verses over a wound, a משנה already says this person loses עולם הבא. So calling it merely 'forbidden' seems too mild. The two sources seem to disagree about the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather, then (following an answer to its result)
One who whispers (verses or a charm)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying healing is permitted. It is asking why רבי יהושע בן לוי called it only 'forbidden' when the משנה gives a much harsher result.

phrases.english: But then, when he said it is forbidden,
it was where there is a wound?
If there is a wound,
is it just forbidden, and nothing more?!
But we learned: One who whispers over a wound
has no share in the World to Come!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא כִּי אָמַר אָסוּר דְּאִיכָּא מַכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the answer of step 16 to its result and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The understanding that רבי יהושע בן לוי's 'forbidden' refers to whispering over a wound
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה gives that exact act a far harsher outcome (losing עולם הבא), so 'forbidden' seems too mild.

steps.title: The משנה is about someone who spits
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explained that the משנה speaks of someone who spits and then says the verses. That is worse, because ה׳'s name may not be mentioned with spitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it already said about that משנה that רבי יוחנן said: They taught it about one who spits, because one may not mention the name of Heaven over spitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a statement of רבי יוחנן. The harsh משנה is about a worse case: someone who spits and then says the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mixing ה׳'s name with spitting is disrespect toward Heaven, so it gets the harsh punishment of losing עולם הבא. Just saying verses over a wound, without spitting, is only 'forbidden', as רבי יהושע בן לוי said. The two sources describe two different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasn't it already said about it?

phrases.english: Wasn't it already said about it:
Rabbi Yochanan said:
They taught it about one who spits;
phrases.notes: He means someone who spits on the wound and then whispers the verses.

phrases.english: because one may not mention
the name of Heaven over spitting.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּרוֹקֵק שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17 by narrowing the משנה to a worse case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the opposing source (the משנה speaks only of one who spits)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's harsh punishment applies to anyone who whispers verses over a wound.
steps.terutzMaskana: Losing עולם הבא is only for one who spits and mentions ה׳'s name; whispering without spitting is merely forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Three levels: protecting with פסוקים is allowed; healing a wound with them is forbidden; spitting and then saying them costs one his share in עולם הבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sugya sets up the classic distinction between using פסוקים for protection and using them as a cure, and it shows special concern for the honor of ה׳'s name.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the procession
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line: the בית דין walks, and two תודות come after them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the court moves forward, and two thanks-offerings come after them, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה about the procession that adds holiness to an area. It is setting up a question on this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes a ceremony for making a new area part of holy ירושלים or the עזרה. On a plain reading, the בית דין walks first and the two תודות follow. That order is what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: The court (here, the great court of seventy-one)
Thanks-offerings (each comes with loaves of bread)
And so on: the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: The court moves forward
and two thanks-offerings after them, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית דִּין מְהַלְּכִין וּשְׁתֵּי תּוֹדוֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, moving from the discussion of verses for protection back to the משנה's procession.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה describes a procession with the בית דין and two תודות.

steps.title: Does the court really walk in front of the offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the בית דין walks ahead of the תודות. A פסוק in נחמיה shows the leaders walked behind the offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this saying the court walks in front of the thanks-offering? But it is written: 'And after them went הושעיה and half of the princes of יהודה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order in the משנה using a פסוק from נחמיה, where the leaders walk after the thanks-offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, the משנה puts the בית דין first. But the פסוק that this ceremony comes from says the leaders went 'after them', meaning after the תודות. So the plain reading of the משנה seems to clash with the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (introduces a doubtful reading)
But isn't it written...? (brings a פסוק to challenge)

phrases.english: Is this to say that the court
walks in front of the thanks-offering?!
But isn't it written:
"And after them went Hoshaiah
phrases.notes: נחמיה 12:32. 'Them' means the two thanks-offerings from the verse just before.

phrases.english: and half of the princes of Judah"!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּבֵית דִּין קַמֵּי תּוֹדָה אָזְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the plain reading of the משנה quoted in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of the משנה, which puts the בית דין in front of the תודות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק in נחמיה, the source of this ceremony, has the leaders walking after the thanks-offerings.

steps.title: The offerings walk first and the court follows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה: the תודות walk in front, and the בית דין walks behind them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: the court moves forward, and here is how. The two thanks-offerings move ahead, and the court walks behind them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by explaining what the משנה really means, so that it matches the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The court moves forward' is only a heading. The details come next: the תודות lead and the בית דין follows. Now the משנה and the פסוק in נחמיה agree.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (rereads a text)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
The court moves forward,
and the two thanks-offerings move ahead
and the court behind them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בית דין walks in front of the תודות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תודות walk in front and the בית דין follows behind, as in the פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: In the procession, the two תודות go first and the בית דין walks behind them.

steps.title: How exactly did the two offerings walk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the two תודות were arranged as they walked.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did the two thanks-offerings walk?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question about how the two offerings were placed. This sets up a מחלוקת in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know the תודות walk first, the גמרא wants the detail. Were they side by side, or one in front of the other?

phrases.english: How do they walk?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד מְהַלְּכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 21 and asks for more detail about the תודות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact arrangement of the two תודות in the procession.

steps.title: Side by side, or one behind the other
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagree. One says the תודות walked side by side, and the other says one walked behind the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון the son of רבי disagree. One says they walked side by side. The other says one walked behind the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a מחלוקת between two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One opinion puts the two offerings next to each other, both at the front. The other puts them in a line, one ahead and one behind. The גמרא does not say which אמורא holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: One alongside the other, side by side
One behind the other, in a line

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Shimon son of Rebbi:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here means רבי יהודה הנשיא, so this is his son.

phrases.english: one says: one alongside the other,
and one says: one behind the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a מחלוקת: side by side (זו כנגד זו) or one behind the other (זו אחר זו).

steps.title: What 'the inner one' means in each view
steps.stepSummary: In the side-by-side view, 'the inner one' is the תודה closer to the wall. In the one-behind-the-other view, it is the תודה closer to the בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says side by side holds that 'the inner one' is the offering closer to the wall. The one who says one behind the other holds that 'the inner one' is the offering closer to the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how each opinion understands the משנה's word 'the inner one'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה calls one תודה 'inner' and one 'outer'. If they walk side by side, 'inner' means the one nearer the wall. If they walk in a line, 'inner' is the back one, nearer the בית דין walking behind.

phrases.english: The one who says one alongside the other:
"the inner one" is the one closer to the wall.
The one who says one behind the other:
"the inner one" is the one closer to the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר זוֹ כְּנֶגֶד זוֹ הַפְּנִימִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what each side of the מחלוקת in step 23 means by 'inner'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Side by side: inner means closer to the wall. One behind the other: inner means closer to the בית דין (the back one).

steps.title: Why is only the inner one eaten if both walk together?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the inner תודה is eaten and the outer one is burned. That fits the line view, but in the side-by-side view both make the area holy together, so why treat them differently?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: the inner one is eaten and the outer one is burned. This works for the one who says one behind the other. The inner one is eaten because the outer one walked ahead and made the area holy for it. But for the one who says side by side, both make the area holy at the same time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the side-by-side view from the משנה's rule that the inner offering is eaten and the outer one is burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the line view, the front (outer) offering makes the area holy first, so the back (inner) one is in a holy place and may be eaten. In the side-by-side view, both reach each spot together. So there is no reason for one to be eaten and the other burned.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for... (sets up 'but for the other view...')

phrases.english: We learned:
the inner one is eaten and the outer one is burned.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זוֹ אַחַר זוֹ,
phrases.english: It makes sense for the one who says one behind the other:
that is why the inner one is eaten,
because the outer one came before it
and made it holy for it.
phrases.notes: The outer one went first and made the new area holy, so the inner one is now in a holy place.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זוֹ כְּנֶגֶד זוֹ,
phrases.english: But for the one who says one alongside the other,
both of them make it holy together!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הַפְּנִימִית נֶאֱכֶלֶת וְהַחִיצוֹנָה נִשְׂרֶפֶת בִּשְׁלָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two views from steps 23-24 against the משנה, and attacks the side-by-side view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the two תודות walked side by side (זו כנגד זו).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both offerings make the area holy at the same moment, nothing explains why one is eaten and the other burned.

steps.title: The same problem hits the other view too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even in the line view, one תודה alone cannot make the area holy. The משנה requires everything, and even the lenient reading treats the two תודות as one מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, in the view of one behind the other, can one offering alone make the area holy? But we learned that any addition not done with all these steps is not holy! And even for the one who reads 'with any one of all these', these two offerings are one מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the challenge by showing it was built on a wrong idea: that the front offering makes the area holy by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the outer offering makes the area holy first, all alone. But the משנה says an addition is not holy unless it is done with all the steps. Even the opinion that reads 'with any one of these' counts both תודות as one מצוה, so neither works without the other. That means the line view has the same question, and the reason for eating only the inner one must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: And by your own reasoning (turns a question back on the asker)
With any one of all these

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not answer why the inner one is eaten. It only shows that the question applies to both views, because neither תודה makes the area holy alone.

phrases.english: And by your reasoning,
for the one who says one behind the other,
does one alone make it holy?!

phrases.aramaic: הָא ״כׇּל שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשֵׂית בְּכׇל אֵלּוּ״ תְּנַן!
phrases.english: But we learned: "any that was not done with all these"!
phrases.notes: 'All these' means every step the משנה listed: king, prophet, אורים ותומים, the court, the two offerings and song.

phrases.english: And even for the one who says "with any one of all these,"
these two together are one מצוה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זוֹ אַחַר זוֹ חֲדָא מִי מְיקַדְּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption behind the challenge in step 25 by showing it hurts the line view as well.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the outer offering alone makes the area holy, which was the only reason step 25 gave for favoring the line view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both readings of the משנה need both תודות together, as one מצוה, before the area becomes holy. So in either view, neither offering makes it holy alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This clears away a false explanation, so the reason one תודה is eaten and the other burned has to come from something other than which one makes the area holy first.

steps.title: A fresh explanation from רבי יוחנן begins
steps.stepSummary: The word אלא sets aside the explanation that just fell apart, and the גמרא introduces רבי יוחנן, who will offer a new way to understand the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it drops the explanation that just failed and introduces a new one from רבי יוחנן. His actual words come in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 25-26 the גמרא found that neither picture of how the תודות walked explained why one תודה is eaten and the other burned. The word אלא tells us that approach is set aside. רבי יוחנן is about to offer a new way of understanding the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather / instead — signals that the earlier explanation is set aside and a new one is coming

steps.confusionAlert: This line alone does not give רבי יוחנן's answer. It only opens it, so don't try to find a ruling here. Read on to the next line.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 26 showed that the earlier explanation does not hold up, this line sets it aside with אלא and opens a new explanation from רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation replacing a rejected one (introduced by אלא); content follows in the next line
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between the inner and outer תודה depended on how the תודות walked (side by side or one behind the other).
steps.terutzMaskana: That approach is set aside; רבי יוחנן will give a different explanation in the next line.
